For U.S. and U.K. readers

Calories in Indian dishes: estimates by portion

For U.S. and U.K. readers comparing familiar Indian dishes, these source-linked values offer a reference point. Scale a specific food record to the portion you ate; ingredients, cooking method, added oil, and serving size vary.

kcal
/ 100 g

The recipe matters as much as the dish name.

A plain dosa, a filled dosa, and a restaurant dosa may not match the same food record. Dal can be prepared with different ingredients and amounts of oil. The serving beside each meal matters too. Search for the closest description, and treat its value as a reference estimate for that record.

A practical estimate

Three steps for a closer portion.

Keep the food and the amount together. If the closest record still differs from your recipe, the result remains an estimate.

1

Choose a close match

Search by dish and preparation when you can. If a result describes a different recipe, keep looking or use it only as a rough reference.

2

Set the amount you ate

Use a listed serving when it matches, or enter the portion weight in grams. Separate items such as rice, dal, and sides can be estimated individually.

3

Scale the reference value

For a value per 100 g, estimate the portion as: kcal per 100 g × portion grams ÷ 100. Rounding and recipe differences make this an estimate, not a lab measurement.

What to compare

Look beyond a familiar name.

When you search, check whether the record reflects the part of the meal you actually ate.

Preparation: Plain, fried, filled, roasted, or simmered foods can have different ingredients and recorded values. Choose the closest preparation rather than assuming all versions are the same.

Portion: A bowl, plate, or restaurant serving can differ in size. If the suggested serving does not resemble yours, enter a weight in grams when you have one.

Mixed recipes: A curry or mixed dish combines ingredients. If its exact recipe is not listed, the nearest entry may not represent every ingredient or cooking choice. Some records have no usable energy value and remain unavailable instead of being filled with a guess.

Common questions about calorie estimates.

How many calories are in chicken biryani?

One Chicken Biryani record in the QikCal Food Library lists 134.53 kcal per 100 g. At 250 g, that record calculates to about 336 kcal. Recipes and portions vary, so this is a reference estimate, not a value for every biryani.

How many calories are in dal?

One Dal record in the QikCal Food Library lists 84.88 kcal per 100 g. At 250 g, that record calculates to about 212 kcal. Ingredients and recipes vary.

How many calories are in naan?

One Naan record in the QikCal Food Library lists 297.36 kcal per 100 g. At 100 g, that record calculates to about 297 kcal. Size and recipe vary.

How do I estimate calories for a portion?

Multiply the selected food record's kcal per 100 g by the portion weight in grams, then divide by 100. The result is an estimate for that record and amount.
